claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it ever starts.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, the lock only protects an execution once it is actually running, not while it waits to enter a locked stage.

If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it in SUPERSEDED mode can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one in progress.
Setting the CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so that each runs in turn rather than being superseded by a later execution.
AWS CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
Both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` can be set when defining a CodePipeline pipeline with the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link target /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ (the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource API docs) exists.
The AWS CodePipeline user guide page 'concepts-how-it-works' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts-how-it-works.html) documents CodePipeline execution modes.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is described later ('below') in the same page, in the 'Manage the pipeline with Pulumi' section.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
The docs link for the Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check (learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/process/approvals) documents exclusive lock checks on environments.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and covers update conflicts.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's **Approvals and checks** tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the stage acquires an exclusive lock on the environment resource referenced by the stage.
The Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` stage property accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`.
`runLatest` is the default value of the Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` stage property.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock; older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run is run against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack one at a time, in order.
`sequential` mirrors how Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The registry docs page /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists for the `CheckExclusiveLock` resource.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up`, `stack: acme/website/production` (org/project/stack form), and `args: --yes`.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, a `deployment` job with `environment` and `strategy: runOnce: deploy: steps` is valid syntax, and `lockBehavior` is placed at the stage level.
`runLatest` is acceptable for a preview environment where only the newest state matters, but not for a stack where every update needs to land.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes update conflicts.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds", located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" option is 0, which means unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that provides one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
Limiting TeamCity concurrent builds to 1 prevents the build from reaching the point of hitting a Pulumi update conflict.
For Azure Pipelines, serializing Pulumi deployments is done by adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that the deployment job targets.
In Azure Pipelines, the `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage makes runs waiting on an exclusive-lock-protected environment execute sequentially (queued in turn).
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored '#serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
In AWS CodePipeline, the default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored '#serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, the build configuration setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', set to `1`, serializes Pulumi deployment builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored '#limit-concurrent-builds'.
